fault_tolerant_sources.title: Fast Black-Box Quantum State Preparation
roles: geometric precision-index state and individual-bit oracle
capped geometric source and its preparation lineage
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: The explicit exact preparation uses a linear-size unary temporary, binary conversion, and routing cleanup. Logarithmic source-register width is not a logarithmic peak-clean-workspace guarantee. No strict gate-count improvement over the routing variants is asserted.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Trading T gates for dirty qubits in state preparation and unitary synthesis
roles: exact dirty-assisted lookup and complete dirty-bank restoration
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Dirty lookup banks do not replace the initialized output program. The basis-state cancellation identity extends to reference-entangled inputs by linearity. Neither dirty lookup nor the counting method is claimed as new.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Quantum state preparation with optimal T-count
roles: optimal unrestricted state-preparation and diagonal-synthesis benchmarks
ancilla-independent diagonal lower bound used through a frame subfamily
complete multiplexors and geometric layer-error allocation
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: A generic preparation theorem does not prescribe the remaining frame columns. An unrestricted-ancilla result does not supply the clean/dirty tradeoff. Multiplexor synthesis and geometric error allocation are already in Appendix B.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Unitary Synthesis with Fewer T Gates
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Use the published precision-dependent T and ancilla bounds separately. The displayed instruction-word construction uses initialized program registers and does not directly give the stated small-clean/dirty frame theorem.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Optimal T Counts under Sparsity: from QROM to State Preparation and Block Encoding
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Different input families; no generic full-frame or bounded-clean-workspace theorem is imported.

fault_tolerant_claim_policy.audit_scope: Checkpoint 32 primary-source comparison, including Bausch; a bounded technical audit, not certification of priority
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.model: Approximate coherent Clifford+T synthesis of the prescribed real frame, with a complete initialized-isometry error bound and exact return of arbitrary dirty/reference inputs. Clean and dirty budgets, precision, and Clifford cost are recorded separately.
do_not_claim: invention of optimal unrestricted state preparation or diagonal synthesis
invention of multiplexor synthesis or geometric layer-error allocation
invention of geometric precision indexing or dyadic bit-oracle sampling
invention of dirty lookup, selector cancellation, or borrowed-bit echoes
new finite-width counting or ancilla-independent lower-bound machinery
one circuit simultaneously optimal in CNOT size, depth, and T count
a general constant-clean-workspace frame lower bound from a small-source obstruction
differentiation of the compiled circuit family or optimal gradient-query complexity
priority inferred from absence of a matching result in a bounded search
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.compact_source_role: An explicit exact O(L)-T, O(log L)-peak-clean implementation of the established capped geometric source, with ordinary binary labels and exact temporary return.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.direct_sampler_role: A complete addressed SU(2) compiler using fixed Pauli atoms, geometric bit sampling, charged lookup, and standard oblivious amplitude amplification. Its direct frame composition already yields the matching count in polynomial-precision examples.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.principal_contribution: The structured full-frame, uniform-in-precision upper construction: residual grouping, one shared accepted-branch shift source, failure tracking, and global amplification. Combined with imported lower bounds, it matches T count in the explicitly stated workspace regimes.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.all_clean_budget_corollary: A splice of supported compilers under an additional workspace/precision condition; not a new independent lower bound.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.moderate_precision_boundary: The L=n^2, a=Theta(n), b=Theta(n sqrt(N)) witness is already attained by the earlier direct sampler and must not be presented as an incremental checkpoint-28 gain.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.qbp_bridge: At fixed parameters, complete-isometry and observable-implementation error bound the bias of a bounded-score estimator. No derivative of the classically selected Clifford+T word is taken.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.evidence_boundary: Analytic construction and finite component checks; no general emitted fault-tolerant frame compiler is claimed.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.review_status: Internal source and proof audit; broader independent review remains necessary before submission.

do_not_claim: invention of borrowed or dirty ancillas
novelty of the abstract echo as a general circuit identity
